Postgraduate English Language Proficiency Requirements
and International English Language Equivalencies
Overview
The University of Auckland (UoA) sets standards for English Language proficiency for admission
to the University for international applicants. All international applicants are required to provide
satisfactory evidence of their proficiency in English.
This could be an acceptable English language test, such as IELTS or TOEFL, or previous academic
study completed in English. The purpose of this document is to outline what will be accepted as
satisfactory evidence for this requirement.
Note: Domestic applicants are not included.
Approved by Education Committee in June 2025 and effective for applications received on or after 1 August 2025, for
commencement in Semester 1 2026 and onwards.

English Proficiency Tests
Validity Period - All test results are valid for two years from the date on the test certificate to the
start of the UoA programme. Requirements must be met on one test certificate.
Exceptions - Some programmes have higher requirements; for these please refer to the degree
specific requirements on page 10.

Prior Study in English
Validity Period – Prior study in English is valid for two years from the date you completed your
previous study to the date you begin your study at UoA
The validity period can be extended to five years with evidence of further study in English, English
language work experience, or if you hold a passport from a “predominantly” English-speaking
country 3. The decision to extend the validity period to five years will be assessed on a case-by-
case basis. Completion of the following qualifications with the required English grade will meet our
Postgraduate English Language Proficiency Requirements. Each of these English grades also has
an assigned IELTS equivalency. Some of the programmes below only have IELTS equivalency for
IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0). If you are applying for a programme with a higher IELTS
requirement, you will need to sit one of the approved English proficiency tests on page 3.

3.2 Tertiary Study in the English Medium
For prior tertiary study, applicants are required to meet one of the following requirements:
Sub-doctoral
• A bachelor's degree (minimum 3 years duration); OR
• A postgraduate qualification (minimum of one year duration)
Doctoral
• A bachelor's degree (minimum three years duration); OR
• A postgraduate qualification (minimum one year duration) AND a bachelor's
degree (minimum 3 years duration), with no greater than two years between the
completion of the bachelor's degree and the beginning of the postgraduate study;
OR
• A postgraduate qualification (minimum 2 years duration)
Approved by Education Committee in June 2025 and effective for applications received on or after 1 August 2025, for
commencement in Semester 1 2026 and onwards.

3.3 Qualifications taught in Offshore Campuses
Some universities offer qualifications from their offshore campuses in multiple locations around
the world. Successful completion of qualifications at bachelor's degree level or higher from these
campuses is acceptable for English Language equivalency for admission to postgraduate studies 7.
3.4 Graduate Diplomas from New Zealand Universities and Polytechnic Institutions
Applicants must have completed a one-year full-time Graduate Diploma from a New Zealand
university, or polytechnic institution. Please note that this does not meet the English language
requirement for Doctoral programmes.

4.2 Teaching in English
Experience teaching at a tertiary level in the English medium, for two years or more, in a recognised
university where English is the language of instruction. Please refer to the list of acceptable
countries in Section 3.2. Note: The same validity period which is stated in Section 3 also applies
here.
4.3 Law Applicants from Norway
Applicants from Norway who are applying for postgraduate programmes in law will qualify for
admission and English equivalency provided they have obtained a pass (minimum 4) in Vitnemål
English.

English Language Waivers
Applicants who have not met English proficiency through the above standards may, in some
circumstances, be granted a waiver. An applicant’s eligibility for a waiver to sub-doctoral
programmes will be assessed on a case-by-case basis by Applications and Admissions and may
require further supporting evidence. All applicants who are awarded a waiver will be required to
sit a Diagnostic English Language Needs Assessment (DELNA) no later than two weeks after the
start of their first semester. Any recommended enrichment/support must be undertaken. For
Doctoral applicants seeking a waiver, a recommendation must be submitted by the Academic
Head of the relevant academic unit to the Doctoral Admissions team. All cases will be assessed
on a case-by-case basis.
5.1 English Language Waiver Conditions
Approved by Education Committee in June 2025 and effective for applications received on or after 1 August 2025, for
commencement in Semester 1 2026 and onwards.
8
For a waiver to be considered, an applicant needs a combination of at least two of the following:
• Completion of a bachelor's degree from a university, or polytechnic institution from a
country not listed in Section 3.2. The medium of instruction during this study must have
been English and must not have been completed more than 2 years before the
beginning of study at UoA.
• Completion of a postgraduate qualification (at least one year in duration) 10, or a
bachelor's degree from a university, or polytechnic institution, from one of the
countries listed in Section 3.2. This prior study must have been completed more than
2 years for the countries listed or more than 5 years, for those who are also citizens of
predominantly English-speaking countries, before the start of study at UoA. 11 12. This
means that completed qualifications that fall outside the normal validity periods to meet
English proficiency may be considered in conjunction with other forms of evidence.
• Published research in English where the applicant was the lead researcher and
presented in English at conference(s).
• Evidence of extensive work experience in English.
5.2 Marginal Test Scores
Applicants who have not achieved the required scores in an IELTS, TOEFL or PTE Academic test
may be considered for an English Language Waiver.
IELTS: Where the applicant has submitted an IELTS test, in which one of Speaking, Listening or
the Overall Score components is lower than the minimum requirement by 0.5 points. An IELTS with
a low writing or reading score will not be considered.
TOEFL: Where the applicant has submitted an overall TOEFL score (internet- or paper-based test)
which is lower than the minimum requirement by up to 2 points, but the written English score meets
or exceeds the minimum.
PTE: Where the applicant has submitted an overall PTE result which is lower than the minimum
requirement by up to 8 points, but the communicative score meets the minimum.
